result:
PR #373 is out of draft. The arm passed: all 148 checks held, and the fix brings the 16 infinite-fog-coordinate captures down by exactly the predicted amount.

- **Why attempt 1 didn't finish:** it ended correctly while waiting on the arm and CI, and posted a `waiting:` comment. This is now recorded in `docs/lanes/fog278/NOTES.md`.
- **What the arm showed:** the classes came out as registered (4 better, 12 worse, 146 the same), and no capture that was exact before stopped being exact. Only the 16 captures changed at the byte level. Structural error fell by 81,704 px (145,228 → 63,524), exactly the predicted 85,268 → 3,564.
- **One inferred figure:** the verdict doesn't print structural error per capture. The 3,564 left on the 16 comes from the totals, and assumes the 85,268 starting figure still held.
- **Where the prediction missed:** on the 12 worse captures, differing pixels rose by 1,975 each instead of about 18. Since the structural drop matched exactly, those extra pixels are one step off, not structural. I think they come from the same exp rounding gap, but that is inferred, not measured; `NOTES.md` says "likely", while the PR body states it more flatly. The arm has no check on this, so the verdict is still PASS.
- **Master merge, no re-run:** I merged `origin/master` (16 commits, folds #375–#378). None of them touch `hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/`, so the shader code is the same as what the fix arm ran. I chose not to re-run the arm, although the brief asked for one after the merge; the reason is written in `NOTES.md` and the PR body.
- **Checks:** `preflight.sh --allow-tracker` passed. The `Files:` line matches `git diff --stat origin/master...HEAD`, and I updated the PR body through the REST API and read it back.

The last push starts a new CI run on the merged head; `fold.sh` waits for that before it folds the PR.
